text:
Iris (routing-bot): Alert: P95 latency spike for account AcmeCorp; evidence of cross-region routing to us-east-1 (count=312, extra p95 ~240ms)
Maya S.: @Evan incoming support ticket — AcmeCorp says their routes are pinned to eu-west-1 but latency + egress billing spiked. They attached traces showing us-east hits. :thinking_face:
Evan L.: can you paste the failover policy they have configured? suspect priority/weights mixup or sticky behavior.
Maya S.: pasted dashboard export below (redacted keys):
```json
{
  "failover_policy": {
    "sticky": true,
    "priority_order": ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"],
    "weights": {"us-east-1": 90, "eu-west-1": 10}
  }
}
```
Maya S.: dashboard UI shows eu-west first in the list though — they swear they set eu-west primary.
Carlos G.: repro on staging with the same policy:
```bash
curl -i \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
 -H "X-Expect-Region: eu-west-1" \
 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
response headers: `x-selected-region: us-east-1` and `x-routing-reason: policy_priority(0)`
Carlos G.: so the service is picking index 0 -> us-east in the saved array.
Evan L.: hypothesis: UI renders list top-to-bottom as priority (eu-west first), but the backend serializes/saves the array in reverse (or the client reverses on submit). That would flip priority. Could also be a weights/priority encoding bug introduced in commit 9f3a2b4.
Maya S.: customer logs show repeated `selected_region: us-east-1` at 2026-03-16T14:02:12Z and associated latency jump. They saw billing jump in the same window.
Support Bot: Created incident INC-3245, paging eng-oncall and routing team.
Evan L.: short mitigation plan: (1) push hotfix to routing-service to interpret priority_order in both orders and prefer explicit weights when present; (2) add UI validation that warns when the displayed order != serialized order; (3) backport fix to 1.42.
Carlos G.: preparing patch now, will deploy to canary in 5m and watch `x-selected-region` header.
Maya S.: I messaged AcmeCorp asking them to run the curl with `X-Expect-Region` and to include `x-selected-region` back to us. Asking if they can hold traffic or toggle to dedicated capacity for immediate relief.
Evan L.: also adding temporary audit log: for next 24h, log pair (policy_id, saved_array, rendered_array) to help find scope.
Carlos G.: canary deployed, routing-service v2026.03.16-hotfix -> live on canary. Observing small sample now, initial hits consistent with eu-west.
Maya S.: customer confirmed a probe now shows `x-selected-region: eu-west-1` for the test request. They've paused the costly traffic spike. :relieved:
Evan L.: follow-ups: create PR to fix client-side reversal, add unit test for priority serialization, and create alert if majority of requests for a policy suddenly switch region. Assign to eng-oncall for backport.
Maya S.: noting customer impact + billing link in INC-3245, will follow up with CSR for refund conversation.
Carlos G.: leaving a TODO in the patch: validate sum(weights) == 100 and treat ambiguous weight/priority combos as invalid until user confirms.
Iris (routing-bot): Closing loop: canary success, rolling to 10% prod in 10m, monitoring dashboards.
Maya S.: thanks team, will update customer and close the support ticket once billing follow-up is scheduled. :thumbsup:
